tasks.title: Secrets .env.production
tasks.notes: All production env vars: DB, queue, Stripe, mail, cache. CACHE_STORE=database required.

prep.what: Audit and finalize the `.env.production` file on azteam-vps — confirm every production secret is correct after the deploy: DB credentials, Stripe live keys, mail config, and `CACHE_STORE=database`.
prep.understand: Any missing or wrong env var silently breaks a feature in production. `CACHE_STORE=database` is non-negotiable for `ShouldBeUnique` to work. After any edit, you must rebuild the config cache or the app keeps serving stale config.
approach: On azteam-vps, diff `.env.example` against `.env.production` to spot any missing keys that were added since last deploy.
Verify the critical values: `APP_ENV=production`, `APP_DEBUG=false`, `CACHE_STORE=database`, Stripe live keys (`STRIPE_KEY`, `STRIPE_SECRET`), and mail SMTP credentials.
Run `php artisan config:cache && php artisan route:cache` after any change.
Smoke-test: load fin.azteam.cloud and check logs — no config or key errors.
resources: `.env.example` in the repo — canonical list of all required keys
Stripe dashboard → Developers → API keys (switch to live mode)

tasks.title: deltaPct guard
tasks.notes: Guard division-by-zero on delta percentage calculations across analytics views.

prep.what: Add a zero-denominator guard to every delta-percentage calculation so the app never divides by zero when a prior-period value is 0.
prep.understand: Delta % = (current − prior) / prior × 100. When prior = 0, this crashes or returns infinity. The fix is a null-safe helper that returns `null` when prior is 0, and renders `—` in the UI. One shared helper beats patching each callsite.
approach: Grep the codebase for `deltaPct`, `delta_pct`, or division patterns like `/ $prior` in `app/` and `resources/views/`.
Extract a shared helper: `function deltaPct(?float $current, ?float $prior): ?float { return ($prior && $prior != 0) ? (($current - $prior) / $prior * 100) : null; }`
Replace all inline calculations with the helper.
In Blade/JS, render `null` delta as `—` (em-dash) so the UI stays clean.
resources: Grep: `deltaPct` or `delta_pct` across `app/` and `resources/views/`
PHP null-coalescing `??` and ternary for safe rendering in Blade
Existing number-formatting helpers in `app/Helpers/` if they exist

tasks.title: NotificationChannel abstraction
tasks.notes: t20 (NotificationChannel) is in_progress/partial. This extracts it into a clean interface.

prep.what: Finish the `NotificationChannel` abstraction — an interface that lets email, SMS, and push notifications swap behind a common `send()` contract, building on t20's partial work.
prep.understand: t20 is already partially built — start by reading what's there, don't rebuild from scratch. The goal: notification dispatch code doesn't know which channel it's using. This decoupling lets you add channels later without touching core logic.
approach: Find and read the partial t20 work: grep for `NotificationChannel` in `app/` (check Contracts, Services, Notifications folders).
Finalize the interface: `interface NotificationChannel { public function send(Notifiable $notifiable, Notification $notification): void; }`
Implement concrete classes: `EmailNotificationChannel`, `SmsNotificationChannel` (stub SMS body if SMS isn't fully ready).
Bind the implementations in `AppServiceProvider` and update dispatch code to inject the channel via the container.
resources: Partial t20 work — grep `NotificationChannel` in `app/`
Laravel Notification docs → custom channels section
`app/Contracts/` or `app/Services/` — likely home for the interface
Laravel service container binding docs (`AppServiceProvider::register`)

tasks.title: Conversation + Message models
tasks.notes: Blocks t13, t15, t17. The outbound state machine (t8, in_progress) will drive Conversation.status.

prep.what: Create the `Conversation` and `Message` Eloquent models (plus migrations) — one outreach thread per influencer, with individual messages as the back-and-forth inside it.
prep.understand: This is a foundational blocker for t13, t15, and t17. A `Conversation` is one outreach thread per influencer per campaign; a `Message` is a single send or receive within that thread. The outbound state machine (t8) drives `Conversation.status` through pending → sent → replied → closed.
approach: Design schema: `conversations (id, influencer_id FK, campaign_id FK, platform enum, status enum, started_at)` and `messages (id, conversation_id FK, direction enum [outbound/inbound], body text, sent_at, external_id nullable)`.
Generate migrations: `php artisan make:migration create_conversations_table` and `create_messages_table`.
Generate models: `php artisan make:model Conversation` and `Message` — add `hasMany` / `belongsTo` relationships between them.
Add model factories so tests can seed conversations and messages without manual DB inserts.
resources: t6 agency/influencer schema (in_progress) — check what `Influencer` model already has to align FK naming
t8 outbound state machine (in_progress) — the states it drives map to `conversations.status` enum values
`php artisan make:model Conversation -mf` — generates model + migration + factory in one command
Laravel Eloquent relationships docs — `hasMany`, `belongsTo`

tasks.title: Append-only audit log
tasks.notes: Immutable insert-only log for all state changes. Compliance (LGPD, Stripe) + debug trail.

prep.what: Implement an append-only `audit_logs` table and an `Auditable` trait so every key model can record immutable state-change entries — inserts only, never updates or deletes.
prep.understand: Append-only means the migration has no soft-deletes and the model has only `created_at` (no `updated_at`). Use a polymorphic relation (`loggable_type` / `loggable_id`) so any model can attach audit entries. This underpins LGPD compliance, Stripe audit trail, and debugging the outreach state machine.
approach: Create `audit_logs` migration: `(id, loggable_type, loggable_id, event varchar, actor_id nullable FK, payload JSON, created_at)` — no `updated_at`, no soft-delete column.
Create `AuditLog` model: set `public $timestamps = false`, add `$fillable`, add `loggable()` morphTo relationship.
Create `Auditable` trait with a `logAudit(string $event, array $payload = [])` helper that creates an `AuditLog` record bound to `$this`.
Apply `use Auditable` to the first consumers: `Influencer` (from t6) and `Conversation` (built today in t29).
resources: Laravel polymorphic relationships docs — `morphTo` / `morphMany`
t9 DEK encryption (in_progress) — sensitive `payload` fields may need to reference its key strategy
t6 Influencer model — first consumer of the trait
`php artisan make:model AuditLog -m` — scaffolds model + migration together
